behavior.explanation: Two source-visible privileges alter only who may query. A site administrator passes because ctx.Doer.IsAdmin is true. A current-repository administrator passes because ctx.IsUserRepoAdmin() returns ctx.Repo.Permission.IsAdmin(). Either may query a different collaborator. After that bypass, the target of permission computation remains the resolved collaborator and current repository. Caller privilege is not copied into the result. Separately, inside GetIndividualUserRepoPermission, if the queried collaborator is themselves a site admin or is the repository owner, that queried collaborator receives AccessModeOwner.

observations.subject: normally authenticated caller querying self

behavior.explanation: For the same normally authenticated, nonprivileged caller querying another username, the self comparison differs from the own-query case: it is false. If the caller is also neither a site admin nor an admin of the current repository, GetRepoPermissions returns forbidden immediately. It does not look up the other user and does not compute or disclose that user's repository permission. If 'normal' was not intended to exclude repository-admin or site-admin status, the privilege branches below remain applicable.

behavior.explanation: Two source-visible privileges alter only who may query. A site administrator passes because ctx.Doer.IsAdmin is true. A current-repository administrator passes because ctx.IsUserRepoAdmin() returns ctx.Repo.Permission.IsAdmin(). Either may query a different collaborator. After that bypass, the target of permission computation remains the resolved collaborator and current repository. Caller privilege is not copied into the result. Separately, inside GetIndividualUserRepoPermission, if the queried collaborator is themselves a site admin or is the repository owner, that queried collaborator receives AccessModeOwner.
